summary: Verified new JWT auth, per-user project history, follow-up chat with memory, cross-user isolation, navigation (studio/kit/guide), and responsive (390px) menu behavior for the Anti Generic Engine. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases passed (register/login/me/lockout, analyze public, project isolation, cross-user 404, protected-endpoint 401, chat persistence on demo project). Frontend: demo login, reload persistence, history open, 6 stage tabs, project chat (assistant reply + memory counter '3 EXCHANGES SAVED'), rename, new-project reset, nav flows, logout, duplicate-email register error, mobile open/close menu, fresh-user history-empty state — all pass. No crashes, no console errors during happy paths (only the expected 409 on duplicate register).
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py check_lockout: identifier keyed by client.host + email. Behind proxies (e.g. Cloudflare) all users may share the same client.host, so a single attacker can lock out other users of the same email. Consider using X-Forwarded-For or keying by email only with a longer window.
auth.py: password minimum length is 6 (very weak). Consider raising to 8+ and enforcing complexity.

server.py: /api/workflow can spend 60-150s inside a single request without a client-cancellation guard; a client disconnect still runs all six LLM calls. Consider background task + polling, or an early cancellation check.
server.py stream_llm: creates a new session_id per call, so LlmChat cannot leverage server-side context between stages — context is only replayed via prompt. Working correctly but noted.

Short-password on the register form is enforced only via the browser's native minLength popup; the client never round-trips to receive the 422 array. This is fine, but the auth-error component should still be resilient to receiving an array detail from the backend (recommend always coercing to string before render if not already).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_auth_and_projects.py (parallelized). The full 6-stage /api/workflow build is expensive (~60-150s) and is NOT covered by pytest to save time; it is exercised implicitly by reusing the demo project for chat/history assertions. If you need to test the build itself, budget ~180s and add a single test with a generous timeout. Note: the demo project title was mutated during frontend tests (rename) — this is expected and safe to leave. Cloudflare on the preview URL accepts a browser-like UA (test file sends 'Mozilla/5.0 pytest-backend' and works). Password lockout is IP+email keyed; running the lockout test many times in a row may temporarily 429 subsequent logins from the same host — the fixture registers a fresh email each run to avoid contaminating the demo account.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues found in this iteration.
